pattern: Supplementary preview disclosed on hover or keyboard focus, meeting WCAG 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus; the card is a generic container in DOM order right after the trigger (not a dialog, not a tooltip).

aria.value: id of the card, added to existing ids while describe is true (default); removed on describe false and destroy()

keyboard.action: Moves into focusable card content (the card follows the trigger in the DOM); the card stays open.
Hides the card (reason focus-out) unless the pointer is over it.

keyboard.context: Card visible and topmost, focus on the trigger or elsewhere
keyboard.action: Hides the card without moving focus (reason escape); it stays hidden until pointer or focus leaves and returns.
Hides the card and moves focus to the trigger; it does not reopen until focus leaves and returns.
Closes only the card; the next Escape reaches the dialog.

focus: Showing never moves focus. Focus inside the card or keyboard focus on the trigger keeps it open. Escape or hide() with focus inside the card returns focus to the trigger; focus-out, pointer-leave, and outside-pointer closes leave focus where the user put it.
notes: 1.4.13 dismissible: Escape hides the card without moving pointer or focus off the trigger, and it stays dismissed until the pointer or focus leaves and returns.
1.4.13 hoverable: the pointer can move from the trigger onto the card within hideDelay; the card stays open while hovered.
1.4.13 persistent: stays visible while trigger or card is hovered or focused, until Escape, an outside press, or another hover card opens.
DOM order places the card right after the trigger, so reading and Tab order follow the visual relationship (1.3.2, 2.4.3).
Only one hover card is visible at a time; touch pointers never open it, so it must not hold essential information or actions.
With describe true the whole card text becomes the trigger's description; use describe false for long or interactive cards.
knownCaveats: Manual screen-reader verification (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) is pending.
The card has no role or name; screen-reader users discover it only through aria-describedby (describe true) or by tabbing into it.
